t: The Keira sultans ruled Darfur from Jebel Marra for over 250 years, building an Islamic state in the eastern Sahel.
Its Forty Days Road carried slaves, ivory and feathers to Egypt, and West African pilgrims passed through it to Mecca.
Conquered in 1874 and revived in 1898, it fell to an Anglo-Egyptian force with aircraft in 1916.
dyk: Much of what we know of the sultanate's court comes from Muhammad al-Tunisi, a Tunisian traveller who lived in Darfur from about 1803 to 1811.
ev: Suleiman Solong unites the Fur under the Keira dynasty
Ahmad Bukr begins his reign and makes Islam the religion of the state
Sultan Abd al-Rahman fixes the royal court at El Fasher
Egypt conquers Kordofan, cutting Darfur's eastern trade
Al-Zubayr defeats Sultan Ibrahim at Manawashi and Darfur is annexed by Egypt
Ali Dinar returns to El Fasher and restores the sultanate
Anglo-Egyptian force wins at Birinjiya; Ali Dinar is killed in November
